phase0_step5_threat_ceiling.rationale: RULES maps 49 (from,to) pairs onto only 4 threat levels, so a wrong recovered pair can still yield the correct threat -- exact-pair accuracy is a pessimistic lower bound on the number that actually gates end-to-end tactical accuracy.

phase0_step6_decompose_failures.verdict: reduction/guard logic, not classifier accuracy, is the dominant bottleneck: 47.2% of failures had zero misclassified windows yet still failed, and filtering to correct-only windows recovers the pair in only 0.9% of failures. dispersed_converging_ambiguity (stgt_bridge.py, unconditional, fires across all formation classes, previously documented unfixed in AUDIT.md sec AG) is the single largest cause at 60.9%. Chain-length-2 (real transitions) has NEVER succeeded once (0/251) -- every one of strategy 5's 62 successes is a steady state. Retraining (strategy 6) is unlikely to move the pair ceiling much on its own since the dominant blocker is bridge/reduction-code logic, not training data -- flagged, not acted on (out of scope this turn); proceeding to strategy 6 exactly as instructed.
